title.narrative: Activity 09: Kenya National Committee Seminar on Policing and the Prevention of Identity-based Violence

description.narrative: The Kenya National Police Services training on the Prevention of Electoral Violence as an aspect of Identity-based Violence Prevention. The training was conducted in the aftermath of COVID-19 related lockdowns. The Africa Programs Office (APO) developed a hybrid format, where the participants and local resource persons attended the training in-person, while resource people from outside Kenya conducted the training, facilitated group work and other seminar activities through zoom. The training targeted 25 participants during the second week of November, who included mid-level officers working in locations where recordings of the “Never Again” documentary were conducted. The goal was to be able to effectively disseminate learning from the documentary towards critical players and stakeholders to build their capacity for prevention of especially identity-based and also electoral violence at the local level. Implemented under the theme of “Prevention of Identity-based Violence in the Great Lakes Region, electoral violence and Identity-based violence are characteristic features during genocide and mass atrocity processes. In the past election cycles in Kenya, both have been reported during pre- and post-election experiences, and currently there are threats of a research in the upcoming 2022 elections. The training activities sought to expose participants to processes by which these forms of violence occur, while providing a range of approaches and tools to provide knowledge and skills to facilitate their application in local contexts towards prevention.
